subject: Intermittent timeouts & 5xxs — Nimbus Retail egress path investigation
messages:
From: Adam Liu <adam.liu@nimbusretail.com>

Cc: netops@nimbusretail.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in timeouts and 5xxs since 07/12 02:00 UTC

Hi Ava / Marissa,

We started seeing a surge in 5xx responses and client timeouts to Redwood's hosted inference endpoint around 02:00 UTC this morning. Impact:~25% of requests from our checkout flows returned 504/502 over a 40-minute window; retries pushed CPU in our frontends.

We've collected a couple of tcpdumps and traceroutes from our side (attached). Can you confirm whether Redwood had any maintenance or region failovers? If not, please advise next steps — this is affecting checkout latency and conversion.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Nimbus Retail

Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts and 5xxs since 07/12 02:00 UTC

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Correlated Datadog traces (linked) show outbound RTTs to Nimbus prefixes spiking from our egress NAT cluster around 02:00 UTC — 95th went from ~60ms to ~1050ms for ~35 minutes.
- Observed repeated TCP retransmits and some SYNs with no SYN-ACKs from a transit hop (AS64532) — looks like an intermediate firewall/proxy intermittently dropping state.
- DNS: short bursts of increased lookup latency (~500ms) to Nimbus' resolver IP observed; TTLs are normal. Not seeing authoritative NXDOMAINs.
- Packet capture highlights: multiple flows reset mid-stream; see tcpdump-nimbus-20280712.pcap (attached).

Hypothesis: an upstream transit/firewall (partner edge) is intermittently dropping connections or overloading connection table, causing retries that manifest as 5xxs and timeouts at application layer. Could also be asymmetry on the return path causing packets to be blackholed.

Immediate mitigations we can try:
1) Temporarily route Nimbus traffic through our alternate egress subnet (us-east-1 fallback) — minimal config change, should avoid problematic transit hop.
2) Increase TCP keepalive / extend idle time on the NAT cluster to reduce state churn during transient overload.
3) If customer is amenable, ask Nimbus to confirm no recent firewall rule changes on their side or peering changes with provider AS64532.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the route failover and a condensed pcap summary.

- Rishi
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in timeouts and 5xxs — next steps

Thanks Rishi — good triage. I implemented an immediate temporary policy: routed active Nimbus sessions onto the us-east-1 egress path and updated our route table to prefer the alternate NAT cluster. We also bumped TCP idle timeouts on the NAT cluster from 60s -> 300s.

Early telemetry (10:02 UTC) shows error rate dropping back to baseline; latency 95th reduced from ~1s -> ~120ms for the affected prefix. I'm keeping the route in place while we monitor for 2 hours.

Marissa/Ava: recommend we inform Nimbus that we've applied a routing fallback and are monitoring; ask them to confirm if they see recovery on their side. If Nimbus still sees issues, next step is coordinating with the transit provider AS64532 and Nimbus netops.

I'll compile a short post-incident summary and list of suggested long-term fixes (peer health checks, additional NAT capacity, alternate peering).

— Vivek
VP, Infrastructure Engineering
